keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of people (and any children, elderly, or pets) directly determines total quantities and types of food needed.
Whether this covers only food or also water, cooking equipment, and utensils changes the scale and complexity of the plan.
A set budget caps what can be purchased and may force trade-offs between nutrition, variety, and shelf life.
Storage location and space (apartment pantry vs. garage shelf vs. go-bag) dictates packaging, weight, and portability requirements.
Dietary restrictions, allergies, or strong food preferences determine which products are actually usable in an emergency.
Access to cooking tools or heat sources during an emergency affects which food types (no-cook, just-add-water, canned) are practical.
Knowing whether the goal is a quick first pass or a fully optimised, rotation-scheduled kit sets the right level of effort and completeness.

gold.taskDescription: Assemble a ready-to-use 72-hour emergency food supply that sustains the household through a short-term crisis or disaster.

questions.title: How many people (and pets) does this supply need to cover?
questions.description: Identify the exact number of adults, children, and pets so daily calorie and portion targets can be calculated accurately.

questions.title: Does this include water and gear, or food only?
questions.description: Clarify whether the plan should also cover water storage, a camp stove, utensils, or other supplies beyond food items.

questions.title: What is your total budget for building this kit?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit so recommendations stay realistic and trade-offs between cost, shelf life, and variety can be made.

questions.title: Where will the supply be stored — home pantry, go-bag, or elsewhere?
questions.description: Determine the storage environment (space, temperature, portability needs) to guide choices around packaging size and weight.

questions.title: Are there any dietary restrictions or allergies to work around?
questions.description: Capture any hard dietary requirements — gluten-free, nut allergies, vegetarian, halal, etc. — so every item in the kit is actually safe to eat.

questions.title: Will you have reliable access to heat or cooking during an emergency?
questions.description: Find out whether a stove, camp burner, or only cold water will be available, which determines whether meals need to be no-cook or just-add-water.

questions.title: Is this a quick starter kit or a fully organised, rotation-ready system?
questions.description: Understand the desired level of completeness — a fast first-pass shop vs. a labelled, dated, rotation-scheduled setup — to calibrate effort and detail.
